question: Who must complete a DNR-approved boating education course before legally operating a motorized vessel on Georgia state waters?
choice_a: Any person born on or after January 1, 1998
choice_b: Only persons over the age of 65
choice_d: No one -- boating education is entirely optional in Georgia
explanation: Georgia's mandatory education requirement applies to any person born on or after January 1, 1998, who must complete a DNR-approved boating education course before legally operating a motorized vessel on state waters.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'Mandatory Education Requirement'; confirmed current on Boat-Ed's official Georgia course page

question: Which of these is a recognized exemption from Georgia's mandatory boater education requirement?
choice_a: Owning a boat longer than 40 feet
choice_b: Being licensed by the USCG as a master of a vessel
choice_c: Having a valid driver's license from any state
explanation: A person is exempt from the mandatory education requirement if licensed by the USCG as a master of a vessel, if operating on a private lake or pond, or if a non-resident with proof of an equivalent out-of-state course.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'Mandatory Education Requirement'

question: May a non-resident operate a motorized vessel in Georgia without completing a Georgia-approved course?
choice_a: No, all non-residents must retake a Georgia-specific course regardless of prior certification
choice_b: Yes, but only if they are over 21 years old
choice_c: Yes, if the non-resident has proof of completing a NASBLA-approved boating education course or equivalency exam in another state
choice_d: No, non-residents may never legally operate a vessel in Georgia
explanation: A non-resident is exempt from Georgia's mandatory education requirement if they have proof of completing a NASBLA-approved boating education course or equivalency examination in another state.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'Mandatory Education Requirement'

question: Under what condition may a person less than 12 years of age legally operate a vessel less than 16 feet long powered by a motor of 30 horsepower or less?
choice_b: Only if they have completed a boating education course, with no adult required
choice_d: Only if accompanied by a competent adult
explanation: Persons less than 12 years of age may operate a vessel less than 16 feet long with a motor of 30 hp or less only if accompanied by a competent adult; they may not operate any vessel 16 feet or longer at all.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'Who May Operate a Boat'

question: How does Georgia law define a 'competent adult' for supervising a minor operator?
choice_a: A person age 18 or older who is not under the influence of alcohol or drugs and who is carrying proper identification
choice_b: Any adult family member regardless of age
choice_c: A person age 21 or older with a boating certificate
choice_d: Any licensed driver, regardless of age
explanation: A 'competent adult' is defined as a person 18 years or older who is not under the influence of alcohol or drugs and who carries proper identification.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'Who May Operate a Boat'

question: How may a person 12 through 15 years of age legally operate a PWC or a vessel less than 16 feet long in Georgia?
choice_a: By simply being taller than 5 feet
choice_b: By having passed a DNR-approved boating education course, or by being accompanied by a competent adult
choice_c: There is no way for a 12-to-15-year-old to legally operate a PWC
choice_d: By having a note from a parent, with no other requirement
explanation: Persons 12 through 15 years old may operate a PWC or a vessel less than 16 feet long only if they have passed a DNR-approved boating education course or are accompanied by a competent adult; they may never operate any vessel 16 feet or longer.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'Who May Operate a Boat'

question: What must a person 16 years of age or older have on board to legally operate any boat on Georgia state waters?
choice_a: A certified boating instructor as a passenger
choice_c: Proper identification, such as a driver's license or other government-issued ID containing a description, photograph, and date of birth
choice_d: A notarized letter of parental consent
explanation: Persons 16 or older may operate any boat on Georgia waters if they have proper identification on board -- a driver's license or other government-issued ID with a description, photo, and date of birth.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'Who May Operate a Boat'

question: Because there is no single official DNR-administered boating exam, how do most Georgians actually satisfy the boating education requirement?
choice_a: By passing a written test administered exclusively at DNR regional offices
choice_b: By taking a road test at a Department of Driver Services office
choice_c: There is no way to satisfy the requirement short of a college course
choice_d: By completing a NASBLA-approved course from a DNR-approved provider (such as the online Boat-Ed course DNR itself directs boaters to) or an in-person classroom course
explanation: Georgia has no single state-run boating exam; the DNR directs boaters to complete an approved online course (such as Boat-Ed) or a classroom course through the DNR Boating Education Office, and the vendor's own final exam is what boaters actually complete.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, inside front cover ('Georgia Safe Boating Program'); confirmed on gadnrle.org and boat-ed.com/georgia

question: On the Georgia Required Equipment Checklist, when is the Boating Safety Certificate marked as applicable on board for a PWC operator?
choice_a: If the operator is 12 to 15 years of age
choice_b: Only if the PWC is longer than 16 feet
choice_c: It is never required for PWC operators of any age
explanation: Georgia's required equipment checklist notes the Boating Safety Certificate as applicable on board specifically when the operator is 12 to 15 years of age.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'Georgia Required Equipment Checklist'

question: Can a person less than 12 years of age ever legally operate a vessel 16 feet in length or longer in Georgia?
choice_a: Yes, if accompanied by any adult
choice_b: No, this is prohibited regardless of adult supervision or education course completion
choice_c: Yes, if the child has completed a boating safety course
explanation: Persons less than 12 years of age may not legally operate any vessel 16 feet in length or longer under any circumstance, including with adult supervision.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'Who May Operate a Boat'
